title: Only 7% Pass This Nursing Entrance Exam
summary: Anatomy, vital signs and patient-care decisions test whether your judgement stays sharp under pressure.

landing.intro: Body systems, vital signs and patient care. Can you spot what matters and make the safest call?

about.body:
This worldwide entertainment challenge contains ten entrance-style questions across anatomy, observations, healthcare numeracy, infection prevention, communication and priority judgement. It rewards calm use of the information shown.

Choose the single best answer for each situation. The content stays general and avoids relying on one country's professional procedures.

This is not an accredited nursing entrance exam, clinical assessment, qualification, training course or source of medical advice.

howToPlay.title: How to Play
steps: Complete ten carefully selected questions in one focused challenge.
Choose one answer each time. Correctness remains hidden until the final reveal.
Reveal your result, skill breakdown and complete answer review after the final question.

about.disclaimer: For entertainment and general learning only. This is not an accredited nursing entrance examination, clinical assessment, professional qualification or medical advice. Healthcare procedures and responsibilities vary; always follow local policy and qualified clinical guidance.

checkpoint.finalAdNote: One short ad, then your results.

stage-1.preAdCopy: Your nursing entrance score and three-area breakdown are ready to reveal.

profile-1.title: The Admissions Standout
profile-1.copy: You combined strong foundational knowledge with calm, careful judgement across the entire admissions lab. Details, trends and patient-centred decisions stayed clear even when the cases became more demanding.

profile-2.title: The Nursing Natural
profile-2.copy: You showed an excellent feel for the knowledge and judgement behind safe, compassionate care. Most of the lab’s numerical, observational and communication traps did not pull you off course.

profile-3.title: The Calm Candidate
profile-3.copy: You handled a broad mix of body knowledge, safety decisions and patient scenarios with steady reasoning. A few finer details kept the entrance challenge interesting.

profile-4.title: The Careful Problem-Solver
profile-4.copy: You built a solid result by following the evidence and treating patient safety seriously. Your strongest stage shows where your clinical-learning instincts are already taking shape.

profile-5.title: The Promising Applicant
profile-5.copy: You solved a good share of the admissions lab and showed useful instincts across several care areas. The answer review will reveal which concepts are ready for another look.

profile-6.title: The Compassionate Explorer
profile-6.copy: The lab uncovered some knowledge gaps, but it also found moments of thoughtful, patient-centred judgement. Every reviewed answer is a fresh chance to strengthen the foundations behind safe care.

nurse-r2q5.context: Earlier: breathing comfortably and speaking normally. Now: breathing faster and pausing between short phrases.
nurse-r2q5.question: Which change in this observation note matters most?
answers: The note contains two time points

visual.ariaLabel: Handover says left arm, chart says right arm

nurse-r4q3.question: A task may splash body fluid towards the face. Which protection addresses that stated risk?
answers: No protection if the task is brief

nurse-r6q3.question: Someone asks a sensitive question in a busy public area. What should you do?
answers: Offer to continue the conversation somewhere private
Answer briefly and quietly where you are
Ask nearby people to give you some space
Give only the non-sensitive part of the answer

nurse-r7q1.context: Person A is comfortable with a mildly faster pulse after walking. Person B is suddenly confused, breathing rapidly and looks pale.
nurse-r7q1.question: Who needs attention first?
answers: Person B, because several new signs suggest sudden deterioration
Person A, because their pulse changed
Both can wait for routine observations

nurse-r10q1.question: An airway blockage prevents air reaching the lungs. What downstream effect follows most directly?
answers: The kidneys immediately form more urine

nurse-r10q6.question: Who has immediate priority?
